parsed.title: Freeze-batch receipt omits retained row ids the prose requires
parsed.detail: The freeze-batch paragraph says the receipt 'records the REPLAN-ROUTE branch and every retained (unfolded) row id', but the fixed REPAIR-RECEIPT block has no field for retained row ids — its six fields are Repaired/Refuted-open/Gate/Batch class/Fold diff/Branch. A freeze-batch has nothing folded, so Repaired=none and Refuted/open=none; the retained replan rows have nowhere to be recorded, contradicting the stated contract.

parsed.title: REPLAN-ROUTE hand-off contradicts the REPLAN per-finding verdict hand-off
parsed.detail: The closing-block table now routes freeze-batch to `node scripts/unit-route.mjs <unit>` → planner → `/review-plan` → `/execute-phase`, but the `→ Next:` block still says `any REPLAN (<F1> + <F2> + …) → confirm all proposed SPEC phases, then /execute-phase on this same branch` — skipping the router and the fresh `/review-plan` the table and FOLD_PROCESS step 9 now require. Two hand-offs in the same file disagree.

parsed.title: Allowlist says 'Both resources are normative' after adding a fourth path
parsed.detail: The progressive-loading list was expanded to four numbered paths (ROUTING, planning-preflight, phase-contract, replan-findings) but the closing sentence still reads 'Both resources are normative, one hop from this file, and fail closed when missing.' The count no longer matches the list.

parsed.title: Replan exemption runs the router before the redirect gate, contradicting the gate's 'always first' contract
parsed.detail: The file opens 'Redirect gate (always, before routing)' and plan-feature's turn contract says 'The redirect gate ran FIRST, before any SPEC edit'. The new 'Replan exemption — the router runs first. Before the status gate, run node scripts/unit-route.mjs <NN>' makes the router precede the gate, and on `route: replan` it says 'skip the STOP' — i.e. skip the redirect gate's STOP blocks (planned/in-progress/done/idea). That directly contradicts the gate's own 'No bypass flag exists for this gate' and the turn-contract box.

parsed.title: Router invocation `<NN>` vs `<unit>` inconsistent across the slice
parsed.detail: ROUTING.md and plan-feature SKILL.md invoke `node scripts/unit-route.mjs <NN>` / `<NN>`, while fold-findings, review-change, review-implementation, triage-issue and SENSOR_SIGNALS all invoke `node scripts/unit-route.mjs <unit>`. The router's accepted argument form is never stated, so a documented invocation (`<NN>` vs `<unit>`) is ambiguous and at least one of the two forms is wrong.

parsed.title: plan-fix replan path appends to an existing SPEC but plan-fix's own output contract forbids that
parsed.detail: Step 7 says on `route: replan` the phases 'are appended to the unit's existing SPEC ledger on the same branch instead of a new fix SPEC', yet the Output section and turn contract require `docs/fix/<primary>-<topic>/SPEC.md` with a fresh local commit and hand-off to `/review-plan fix-<primary>`. The skill has no branch for 'existing unit, append only' — its Hand-off block still prints 'SPEC drafted: docs/fix/<primary>-<topic>/SPEC.md' and 'Branch: fix/<primary>-<topic> (local, not pushed)', which is wrong for an in-progress unit on its own branch.

parsed.title: Replan detection runs before ingest but needs the unit folder that ingest resolves
parsed.detail: The new preamble says 'When the target resolves to an existing unit folder, run node scripts/unit-route.mjs <unit> first' and 'run the router before ingest', but step 1 (Ingest) is what resolves the issue numbers and derives the topic/unit; the router needs `<unit>` which is not known until after ingest. The ordering is self-contradictory.

parsed.title: REVIEW-FAIL Next block has a stray orphaned sub-bullet and broken indentation
parsed.detail: The edited block leaves an orphaned fragment: after the adversarial sub-bullet the text reads `...instead of single-reviewer` then a blank line then `       (yes: <which box fired>; no: omit this line)` — a dangling continuation with no owning bullet, plus inconsistent leading indentation (`      ·` vs `     ·`). The fixed block is supposed to be emitted verbatim; as written it is malformed.

parsed.title: REVIEW-FAIL replan line now names `/plan-fix <n>` for a fix, contradicting CLASSIFY's 'never plan-fix'
parsed.detail: The new line says the router 'names the planner (`/plan-feature <unit>` for a feature, `/plan-fix <n>` for a fix)'. But review-implementation/references/CLASSIFY.md (same slice) states replan-in-unit 'never routes to `plan-fix` for a new unit or a new issue (AC 12)' and the fix-now routing says 'never `plan-fix`'. The two documents disagree on whether `/plan-fix` is a valid replan destination.

parsed.title: Owning-stage `plan` hand-off asserts `route: replan` unconditionally
parsed.detail: The table row for owning stage `plan` now reads 'run `node scripts/unit-route.mjs <unit>` → `route: replan`', presenting the router output as a foregone conclusion. A plan-owned finding does not guarantee the router emits `route: replan` (the router decides from the ledger's frozen route); the doc states the output rather than the condition, so a reader following it will treat a non-replan route as an error.

parsed.title: Diagram still routes fix-now to plan-fix, contradicting CLASSIFY's 'never plan-fix'
parsed.detail: The relationship diagram keeps `fix-now ─────────▶ plan-fix ─▶ execute-phase --fix`, while review-implementation/CLASSIFY.md in this same slice states fix-now 'is NEVER a tracked issue and NEVER routes to `plan-fix`' and 'never `plan-fix` (AC 12)'. The triage diagram contradicts the classifier's contract.

parsed.title: New plan-owner signal emits `/plan-feature <unit>` | `/plan-fix <issue>` but the router is the declared owner
parsed.detail: The new trigger says the command is `{command: "/plan-feature <unit>" | "/plan-fix <issue>", ...}` and claims it is 'the same class→destination decision `scripts/unit-route.mjs` owns', yet it bypasses the router and hard-codes the planner. Every other surface in this slice says the router's `route: replan` line names the planner; the sensor duplicates (and can diverge from) that decision instead of emitting the router invocation.

parsed.title: Plan-owner signal fires on 'frozen route is the plan owner' but the ledger schema has no plan-owner route value
parsed.detail: The trigger condition is 'an open row whose frozen route is the plan owner', but the fixed ledger schema quoted in the same file is `| id | file:line | axis | severity | class | route | folded |` and the class vocabulary is fix-now/replan-in-unit/decision-required/proposal/ignore — there is no `route` value meaning 'plan owner'. The sensor cannot mechanically detect the condition it declares, so the trigger is unimplementable as written.
